pages.text: Every block a printer places is paid for in $(l)Filament Units (FU)$(). To make FU, feed raw materials into a $(item)Filament Winder$() to wind them onto a $(item)Filament Spool$(), then Shift+Right Click the spool onto a printer's $(l)side$().$(br2)A material's FU value is derived from its crafting / smelting recipe graph.
Every spool holds $(l)100,000 FU$(), regardless of tier: the tier gates which materials it accepts, not its capacity (see FU Economy).

pages.title: Exact-Tier Winding
pages.text: The winder is strict: a material only winds into a spool of its $(l)exact tier$(). Netherite (Tier 6) needs a Tier 6 spool; cobblestone (Tier 1) needs a Tier 1 spool.$(br2)If the spool's tier doesn't match the material, the winder leaves both untouched.

pages.title: Spending FU
pages.text: At print time the rule relaxes one way: a spool can pay any cost $(l)at or below$() its own tier, never above. High-tier FU covers low-tier blocks (down-converted at the configured ratio); low-tier FU contributes $(l)nothing$() toward higher-tier blocks.$(br2)So a high-tier spool can print a whole stone house, but a Tier 1 spool can never print netherite.

pages.title: Finding a Tier in JEI
pages.text: Every item with an FU value carries a tooltip line like $(l)MC3DP: Tier-5 (50 FU)$(). JEI indexes tooltips, so typing $(l)tier-5$() in its search box lists that whole tier at once: no prefix, no quotes. Any tier from 1 to 8 works.$(br2)The hyphen is deliberate: JEI splits tooltips on spaces, so $(l)tier 5$() would be read as two words and would also match every item whose FU $(o)cost$() contains a 5. One word keeps it exact.
